bullets.title: META's cloud compute announcement triggers sharp AI infrastructure sell-off, debate rages on implications
bullets.body: Meta's reported plan to launch 'Meta Compute'—monetizing excess AI capacity at ~65% utilization—triggered a sharp sector rotation: CRWV fell 14%, NBIS 17%, memory/SOX dropped 6–11%. Debate split between bulls (META monetizing overcapacity improves ROIC, capex unchanged at $175–275B estimates) and bears (signals AI overbuild relative to monetizable demand). JPM, MS, Citi, and Mizuho all reiterated Buy on META; JPM nonetheless downgraded to Neutral citing preference for META developing AI products for its 4B user base.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle intensifying: DRAM +3.1% m/m, supply deficit extends past 2028
bullets.body: UBS raised 2H26 DDR contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q (from +17% prior) and +18% in 4Q; PC DRAM hit $21/Gb in June (+7x YoY). DRAM industry undersupplied until at least 2Q28 with 2027 bit demand growth (+36.2%) far exceeding supply (+19.3%). Memory industry revenues forecast at $992bn in 2026 and $1.76tn in 2027, generating ~$1.2tn FCF. Micron signed 16 multi-year SCAs with price floors; SK Hynix removed price caps. Samsung and SK Hynix announced $3.55tn combined capex through 2040.

bullets.title: June payrolls badly missed at +57k vs 113k consensus; Fed firmly on hold through 2026
bullets.body: June NFP rose just 57k (vs 110-115k consensus), with prior months revised down 74k cumulatively; unemployment fell to 4.2% driven by a sharp drop in labor force participation (-720k), not job creation. Morgan Stanley, Wolfe, and Piper Sandler all see Fed on hold through 2026; implied hike odds for July fell to ~17%. Fed Chair Warsh acknowledged inflation risks 'have come down' at ECB Sintra. Core PCE at 0.21% MoM remains the key threshold—prints above 0.25% would risk a September hike.

bullets.title: S&P 500 posted best quarter since 2020 in Q2; SOX up 88%, best quarter since 1993 inception
bullets.body: The S&P 500 gained +14.87% in Q2 2026 (best since Q2 2020), Nasdaq +21.41%, SOX +87.8% (record since 1993 inception). MU +241.7%, SNDK +257.9% led memory. However, Mag 7 shed $2.3T in June—MSFT -17.2%, AMZN -11.9%, META -10.9%—as AI capex ROI skepticism mounted. Broad market breadth was strong: Russell 2000 +21.15% QTD, equal-weight S&P outpaced cap-weighted by ~300bp in June.

bullets.title: Hedge funds net-sold equities for 3rd straight week; Info Tech at -2.7 SDs, crowding unwinds
bullets.body: GS Prime reported fundamental L/S managers down -1.53% for 6/26-7/2 versus MSCI World +1.67%. Info Tech was most net-sold sector globally for the 4th consecutive week (-2.7 SDs), led by semis/hardware selling. Gross leverage at 313% (85th pct 1-year), net at 79%. JPM Prime noted HF gross leverage peaked at 98th pct (5-year) post-June expiry; tech crowding at +3z and Tech HW above +4z. Early de-grossing flows emerged; seasonality points to continued pressure into late July.

bullets.title: AI capex super-cycle intact but 2027 deceleration risk is real; hyperscaler FCF going negative
bullets.body: Citi's CETS note flags Mag7 AI capex at $1tn+ in 2027 (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT = 90% of spend). Evercore warns hyperscaler FCF is declining and forecast negative with debt/equity issuances rising. AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices ~20% effective July 1 (2nd hike this year); neocloud long-term contract prices moving above $10-12M/MW. Jefferies contrarian bear case: OpenAI costs $8-14k to serve $200 subscriptions; AI revenues concentrated in two private firms with broken unit economics.

bullets.title: DRAM now primary AI supply bottleneck replacing CoWoS; NVDA moves ahead of AVGO as top compute pick
bullets.body: Sunday TMT Playbook (July 5) notes DRAM has replaced CoWoS as the gating factor for chip supply. NVDA moved ahead of AVGO as top mega-cap compute idea due to strong HBM access vs AVGO's 85% fulfillment. TSMC raised 2027/28 capex estimates to $75-80bn. Peter Lee raised 2026 DRAM ASP forecast to +234% YoY (from +200%) and NAND to +236%. HBM demand forecast raised to 33.1bn Gb in 2026 (+90% YoY).

bullets.title: Comcast plans tax-free NBCU/Sky spinoff; CHTR in talks with SpaceX on mobile—media M&A wave looms
bullets.body: Comcast announced separation of NBCUniversal and Sky into an independent public company (~1 year timeline), with Cavanagh to lead NBCU and Angelakis to lead cable RemainCo. CHTR simultaneously held exec-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile partnership. Wolfe Research skeptical spin completes—expects merger of one/both units with peers instead. CMCSA +22% and CHTR +9% on news. SOTP analysis suggests ~$29/share value unlock for CMCSA.

bullets.title: Broad market broadening: equal-weight S&P at ATHs, Russell 2000 best relative start since 2003
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm broad market strength beneath the AI-concentration narrative: NYSE breadth at all-time highs, equal-weight S&P (RSP) set fresh ATH, Russell 2000 up 23% YTD/+11.2% in Q2 (best relative since 2003). Mag 7 on equal-weight basis up only 50bps YTD. Morgan Stanley notes median S&P 1500 stock delivering double-digit earnings growth, fastest since post-COVID boom. Citi lifted S&P 500 year-end target to 8100 ($350/$400 EPS for 2026/27).

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh signals dovish tilt on AI, moving away from forward guidance
bullets.body: Warsh at ECB Sintra expressed 'cautious optimism' on AI productivity gains, said inflation expectations and risks 'have come down' over the past four weeks, and signaled desire to eliminate dot plot/forward guidance. Morgan Stanley expects Fed on hold through all of 2026. A task force co-chaired by former BoE Governor King will focus on real-time economic data. The Supreme Court 5-4 upheld Fed independence in Trump v. Cook, removing tail risk to FOMC.

bullets.title: Oil cratered 20%+ in Q2; Iran-US MoU removing energy tail risk, Hormuz traffic normalizing
bullets.body: Brent fell >20% in Q2 following Iran-US MoU (June 17) extending a 60-day ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Gasoline prices still ~16-28% above pre-conflict levels despite crude normalization. OPEC+ agreed to a 188k bpd output increase effective August. JPM cut 2H26 Brent to $75/bbl (from $85/90) and MS lowered 2027 to $70/bbl. Iran de-escalation removes acute energy inflation and global growth headwinds that had pressured ECB/BoE/Fed.

bullets.title: IT Services sector down ~30% YTD as Big Tech embeds AI engineers directly into enterprise
bullets.body: MS notes IT Services (ACN, Capgemini peers) down ~30% YTD as software vendors encroach on consulting turf. MSFT announced a $2.5bn 'Frontier Company' initiative with 6,000 embedded AI experts; AWS launched a $1bn Forward-Deployed Engineering organization. Morgan Stanley reiterates Underweight on Tieto at 17-34% premium to ACN/Capgemini peers. The trend of software companies doing hands-on AI transformation threatens dedicated IT Services firms' revenue model.

bullets.title: Software sector bifurcates: Security +6%, Apps/IGV -14% in June; infrastructure outperforms
bullets.body: KeyBanc notes infrastructure-exposed software (MSFT, ORCL, NET) returned +18.5% YTD vs apps down -26.5%; large-cap software down 33.5% equal-weighted. Wolfe's Zukin flags MDB, DDOG, SNOW as longs on AI tailwinds; Guggenheim upgraded CRM and NOW to Buy; Wolfe all-SaaS index at 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales. IGV down 16.5% YTD vs S&P +7.5%.

bullets.title: MSFT FY27 FCF could go negative as memory/capex costs surge; Wolfe cuts PT to $525
bullets.body: Wolfe Research cut MSFT PT from $570 to $525 (still Outperform, 34% upside) as memory price increases force FY27 capex to $270bn (+$40bn). FY27 FCF now forecast at -$17.4bn (vs prior +$14.7bn). FY27 gross margin lowered to 63.1% vs consensus 66.6%. Azure growth raised to 41% FY27. MSFT trades at 19x CY27 P/E, a 20% discount to mega-cap peers. Separately, MSFT planned job cuts affecting <2.5% of workforce.

bullets.title: AAPL raising device prices 15-25% on memory cost squeeze; sourcing talks with Chinese CXMT
bullets.body: Apple raised MacBook/iPad/accessory prices 15-25% citing unprecedented memory cost pressures (DRAM up 7x YoY). CEO Cook stated he has 'never seen component price increases this significant.' AAPL simultaneously lobbying Washington to buy chips from CXMT (on Pentagon blacklist) to diversify supply. iPhone 17 production cut ~15% on lower shipment forecasts; iPhone 18 price hikes expected in September. Chinese smartphone makers (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo) cut 2026 shipment targets by up to 30%.

bullets.title: GOOGL PT raised to $415 on 9GW compute capacity in 2028; Google Cloud to hit $300bn revenue
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Nowak raised GOOGL PT from $375 to $415, modeling 9 GW incremental capacity in 2028 (7 GW TPU + 2 GW NVIDIA GPU) and 4 GW of TPU merchant sales. Google Cloud projected to grow 106%/44% in 2027/2028, reaching $300bn+ revenue. Google Cloud EBIT forecast at $132bn in 2028 (~46% of total company EBIT). 2027/2028 capex raised to $350bn/$375bn. GOOGL trades at 18x 2028 EPS vs 21x LT average.

bullets.title: Retail trading at all-time highs; retail investors bought dip in MU, SNDK at record pace
bullets.body: JPM Retail Radar shows retail inflows at 75th percentile last week, with single-stock demand at 94th percentile. MU topped purchases at $897M (+3.7z) after SCAs news; SNDK second at $705M (+4.6z). Combined MU+SNDK retail semis demand at highest in 14+ months. NVDA accumulated $492M. Retail is net buyers of equities with $36bn in flows last week (89th pct 1yr). Citi data: S&P 500 up 12.2% YTD with retail Mag7 interest at 4-year lows (6% of volumes).

bullets.title: ECB likely to hike once more in September as Eurozone PMI recovery broadens; EU GDP upgraded
bullets.body: JPM raised EU growth forecasts on lower inflation (headline fell to 2.8% YoY in June from 3.2% in May), stronger employment (+0.8% annualized in 2Q), and accelerating lending (+3.5% YoY). Germany's 33-reform package could lift trend growth 20-30bp. ECB's Lagarde maintained hawkish bias; JPM sees one final 25bp hike in September as 'very likely.' Eurozone composite PMI revised up to 50.0, consistent with ~0.8% annualized growth.

bullets.title: Debasement trade roars back post-soft NFP: gold targets cut but long-term bullish; dollar firmer
bullets.body: JPM notes debasement trade (Gold+, Dollar-, steeper curve) reignited after soft NFP and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish-to-dovish commentary. Gold base case $4,300/oz 3Q26, $4,500/oz 4Q26—but targets revised down from $6,000 prior as Hormuz normalization removes energy tail risk. Gold down 12.1% in June (worst month since June 2013). Bitcoin at lowest 60-day volatility in cycle; below $60K level implies move to $40K per Hedgeye. JPM broad dollar index up 2.0% in June.

bullets.title: Power/data center buildout accelerating: BE expands Brookfield partnership 5x to $25bn; ERCOT Batch Zero advances
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield from $5bn to $25bn (5x), implying 5GW development potential. OKLO received DOE final safety analysis approval targeting July 2026 first criticality. ERCOT Batch Zero approved with ~35GW baseload and ~65GW study demand supporting IPP contracting. NRG secured 5.4GW H-class turbines from GEV. Data center construction revisions: starts up 113% and power projects up 117% on trailing 6-month basis.
